claims.statement: Initial ITP evaluation uses history, examination, blood count and expert smear; a compatible isolated pattern does not require routine diagnostic marrow sampling.
claims.limitation: One adequate diagnostic consensus. Atypical features, treatment failure or surgical reassessment may justify marrow assessment.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults matching the constrained splenic-disease or asplenia case, not every hematologic disorder.

claims.statement: HIV and hepatitis-C testing help identify secondary causes in suspected adult ITP even without reported exposure risks.
claims.limitation: One adequate diagnostic consensus. Negative tests neither establish primary ITP nor mandate marrow sampling.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults matching the constrained splenic-disease or asplenia case, not every hematologic disorder.

claims.statement: Routine platelet-antibody testing is not the principal diagnostic confirmation for typical ITP; selected assays may assist difficult specialist cases.
claims.limitation: One consensus publication; no assay performance numbers taught.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults matching the constrained splenic-disease or asplenia case, not every hematologic disorder.

claims.statement: When clinically feasible, elective ITP splenectomy is deferred at least one year after diagnosis because remission remains possible.
claims.limitation: ASH 2026 feasible-delay good-practice statement; 2019 consensus suggests 12-24 months. Neither mandates surgery at one year.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults matching the constrained splenic-disease or asplenia case, not every hematologic disorder.

claims.statement: Observation may suit an otherwise stable adult with platelet counts at least 30 x 10^9/L and absent or minor bleeding after considering additional bleeding risks and planned procedures.
claims.limitation: Current publication retains older treatment threshold. Constructed patient values are not new cutoffs.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults matching the constrained splenic-disease or asplenia case, not every hematologic disorder.

claims.statement: Splenectomy can be considered in chronic primary ITP after failure or intolerance of multiple adequate medical therapies or when avoiding chronic medication is a major goal.
claims.limitation: Consideration, not universal superiority or guaranteed remission.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults matching the constrained splenic-disease or asplenia case, not every hematologic disorder.

claims.statement: Indicated pneumococcal, meningococcal and Hib vaccines are coordinated at least 14 days before elective splenectomy when feasible.
claims.limitation: Not a reason to delay lifesaving surgery; not all vaccine series finish in this interval.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults matching the constrained splenic-disease or asplenia case, not every hematologic disorder.

claims.statement: An adult with anatomic or functional asplenia who has not previously received Hib vaccine is recommended one Hib dose.
claims.limitation: One federal authority. HSCT revaccination is a different pathway.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults matching the constrained splenic-disease or asplenia case, not every hematologic disorder.

claims.statement: An adult who has received PCV20 or PCV21 does not routinely receive an additional pneumococcal vaccine dose under the checked CDC guidance.
claims.limitation: Two CDC pages are one authority; recheck at publication.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults matching the constrained splenic-disease or asplenia case, not every hematologic disorder.

claims.statement: PCV15 in an adult without prior PPSV23 is normally followed by PPSV23 at least one year later; selected risk states permit a shorter minimum.
claims.limitation: Case is well beyond the standard interval and does not test the shorter exception. One authority.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults matching the constrained splenic-disease or asplenia case, not every hematologic disorder.

claims.statement: MenACWY does not supply serogroup-B coverage; asplenia creates a risk-based MenB indication beyond routine young-adult shared-decision ages.
claims.limitation: One federal authority; product/history determine the high-risk primary series.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults matching the constrained splenic-disease or asplenia case, not every hematologic disorder.

claims.statement: With ongoing high risk, CDC recommends a MenB booster one year after the primary series and further boosters every two to three years.
claims.limitation: One authority. Same brand; do not restart an adequate series.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults matching the constrained splenic-disease or asplenia case, not every hematologic disorder.

claims.statement: Anti-B-cell therapy impairs non-live vaccine response; CDC advises waiting at least six months after treatment, sometimes longer depending on recovery.
claims.limitation: Does not imply non-live vaccines are intrinsically unsafe, or prescribe a repeat rituximab course.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults matching the constrained splenic-disease or asplenia case, not every hematologic disorder.

claims.statement: Aplastic crisis can abruptly worsen hereditary-spherocytosis anemia; a falling reticulocyte response indicates impaired production rather than simply increased splenic red-cell destruction.
claims.limitation: One current specialist guideline. Constructed reticulocyte values are not cutoffs and do not prove a pathogen.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults matching the constrained splenic-disease or asplenia case, not every hematologic disorder.

claims.statement: Hereditary-spherocytosis splenectomy decisions depend on persistent clinical severity, transfusion burden and functional impairment, not one acute low hemoglobin.
claims.limitation: Adult decisions use specialist guidance; cross-check cohort is pediatric. Operation type not ranked.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults matching the constrained splenic-disease or asplenia case, not every hematologic disorder.

claims.statement: Symptomatic gallstones support cholecystectomy in hereditary spherocytosis; an otherwise compensated splenic course does not acquire a separate splenectomy indication from gallstones alone.
claims.limitation: No asymptomatic-gallbladder prophylactic operation ranking.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults matching the constrained splenic-disease or asplenia case, not every hematologic disorder.

claims.statement: Splenectomy may correct hereditary-spherocytosis anemia and biochemical hemolysis while abnormal red-cell morphology persists because the membrane defect remains.
claims.limitation: One current specialist guideline; smear is not a substitute for clinical response.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults matching the constrained splenic-disease or asplenia case, not every hematologic disorder.

claims.statement: Negative preoperative accessory-spleen imaging does not remove the need for operative inspection for accessory tissue during ITP splenectomy.
claims.limitation: Expert-opinion surgical guidance; no sensitivity or search-completeness percentage asserted.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults matching the constrained splenic-disease or asplenia case, not every hematologic disorder.

claims.statement: Methotrexate is a usual initial disease-modifying treatment for Felty syndrome; arthritis control by a TNF inhibitor does not establish control of neutropenia and infections.
claims.limitation: One adequate open synthesis; underlying reports/series are limited. No dose or required duration authored.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults matching the constrained splenic-disease or asplenia case, not every hematologic disorder.

claims.statement: G-CSF can improve neutrophils during active infection in Felty syndrome; glucocorticoids are generally avoided during infection and disease-modifying agents act more slowly.
claims.limitation: One adequate open synthesis. Hospital infection treatment is already underway; no G-CSF dose or ANC target taught.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults matching the constrained splenic-disease or asplenia case, not every hematologic disorder.

claims.statement: Splenectomy is an option to consider for Felty syndrome with recurrent infections despite adequate medical treatment; durable infection control is not guaranteed.
claims.limitation: One open synthesis with heterogeneous historical evidence; hospital multidisciplinary consideration, not a mandatory operation.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults matching the constrained splenic-disease or asplenia case, not every hematologic disorder.

claims.statement: Pathogenic gain-of-function PIEZO1 variants can produce hereditary xerocytosis with red-cell dehydration and chronic hemolysis.
claims.limitation: No exact mutation, laboratory cutoff or genotype severity prediction invented.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults matching the constrained splenic-disease or asplenia case, not every hematologic disorder.

claims.statement: Splenectomy is avoided in hereditary xerocytosis because limited hematologic benefit and thrombotic risk differ from the usual hereditary-spherocytosis balance.
claims.limitation: Guideline supports management; primary study cross-checks identity and thrombotic association.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults matching the constrained splenic-disease or asplenia case, not every hematologic disorder.

claims.statement: Splenectomy carries lasting infection and thrombosis risks; preventive vaccination and education about fever remain relevant after hematologic improvement.
claims.limitation: General preventive boundary, not an exact antibiotic regimen, prophylaxis duration or measured risk estimate.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults matching the constrained splenic-disease or asplenia case, not every hematologic disorder.

claims.statement: A liquid unilocular or bilocular splenic abscess without internal septations can be suitable for percutaneous drainage; its less invasive burden can matter when operative risk is high.
claims.limitation: One adequate government guidance source. No clinical success percentage, numeric size cutoff, antibiotic regimen or required trial duration inferred. Specific operative choice needs clinician review.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with confirmed nontraumatic pyogenic splenic abscess in an outside hospital; the clinic reviews the record.

claims.statement: Multiple splenic abscess collections can favor operative source control rather than percutaneous drainage; treatment selection depends on collection anatomy, not size alone.
claims.limitation: One adequate government guidance source. No clinical success percentage, numeric size cutoff, antibiotic regimen or required trial duration inferred. Specific operative choice needs clinician review.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with confirmed nontraumatic pyogenic splenic abscess in an outside hospital; the clinic reviews the record.

claims.statement: A platelet response observed during TPO-receptor-agonist treatment does not by itself establish medication-free ITP remission.
claims.limitation: Case-level interpretation of constructed treatment interruption/resumption, cross-checked against the previously verified treatment/remission distinction. This is not a dosing, tapering or mandatory drug-sequence rule. Fresh PMC retrieval was blocked; original source dates and prior verification are retained.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified ITP course or anatomic asplenia; exact patient observations remain constructed data.

claims.statement: For continuing asplenia risk in adults, the MenACWY primary course is followed by boosters at five-year intervals.
claims.limitation: One government authority represented by two pages; not independent clinical studies. Adult high-risk schedule, not a childhood or outbreak dosing rule.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified ITP course or anatomic asplenia; exact patient observations remain constructed data.

claims.statement: A combined MenACWY/MenB vaccine is used when both vaccine components are indicated at the same visit.
claims.limitation: One government authority. Does not make a combined product superior to compatible separate vaccines when both are due; the counterfactual explicitly preserves that overlap.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified ITP course or anatomic asplenia; exact patient observations remain constructed data.

claims.statement: MenB primary and booster doses retain the same vaccine product rather than interchanging Bexsero and Trumenba.
claims.limitation: One CDC authority; distinct MenB products are not treated as interchangeable maintenance doses.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified ITP course or anatomic asplenia; exact patient observations remain constructed data.

claims.statement: The MenB component in Penbraya is the Trumenba product.
claims.limitation: One CDC authority; this component mapping does not by itself establish an indication for the combined vaccine.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified ITP course or anatomic asplenia; exact patient observations remain constructed data.

claims.statement: An extended interval between vaccine doses does not by itself require restarting the series.
claims.limitation: Government general adult schedule instruction; still verify each product, valid prior administration and applicable minimum intervals.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified ITP course or anatomic asplenia; exact patient observations remain constructed data.

claims.statement: The splenic hilum is the most common location represented for an accessory spleen in this approved anatomy concept.
claims.limitation: The package intentionally omits an exact prevalence estimate and does not turn this common-location teaching point into a complete operative search rule.
claims.applicablePopulation: Patients represented by the approved clinic discussions surrounding referral for hospital splenectomy.

claims.statement: A common accessory-spleen location does not establish that inspection of that one location alone is sufficient during splenectomy.
claims.limitation: This concept does not address retained accessory tissue, recurrent hemolysis, completion splenectomy, reoperation, or any operative-management sequence.
claims.applicablePopulation: Learners applying the narrow location-recognition concept rather than an operative-management protocol.

claims.statement: Before elective splenectomy, indicated pneumococcal, meningococcal, and Hib vaccines should be reviewed and given at least 14 days before surgery when possible.
claims.limitation: This does not reproduce product schedules or delay an urgent operation.
claims.applicablePopulation: Stable adults preparing for elective splenectomy.

claims.statement: Fever in a person with impaired splenic function requires immediate emergency assessment; a patient-specific standby oral antibiotic plan does not replace emergency presentation or prompt parenteral treatment after evaluation.
claims.limitation: The case does not select a drug, dose, diagnosis, or outpatient test pathway.
claims.applicablePopulation: Known asplenic adults with new fever.

claims.statement: Felty syndrome is suggested by long-standing, usually seropositive rheumatoid arthritis with persistent neutropenia; splenomegaly is a characteristic supporting feature and recurrent infections may be the presenting problem.
claims.limitation: The pattern is not pathognomonic. The approved diagnostic vignette explicitly excludes medication, infection, and clonal large-granular-lymphocyte causes before asking for the syndrome.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with established rheumatoid arthritis and persistent otherwise-unexplained neutropenia.

claims.statement: Splenomegaly is common in Felty syndrome but is not an absolute prerequisite; persistent neutropenia in the appropriate rheumatoid-arthritis context remains the essential hematologic feature.
claims.limitation: A normal-sized spleen does not establish Felty syndrome and does not remove the need to investigate alternative causes of neutropenia.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with rheumatoid arthritis and persistent neutropenia after alternative causes have been evaluated.

claims.statement: T-cell large granular lymphocytic leukemia and other hematologic, infectious, autoimmune, and medication-related causes can resemble Felty syndrome and require explicit exclusion rather than diagnosis from the triad alone.
claims.limitation: This package does not teach the complete hematologic workup or a separate T-LGL diagnosis concept.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with rheumatoid arthritis, neutropenia, and possible splenomegaly undergoing diagnostic evaluation.

claims.statement: Methotrexate is the usual first-line disease-modifying treatment for confirmed Felty syndrome when treatment is indicated, with specialist monitoring of blood counts and clinical response.
claims.limitation: Felty syndrome is rare and treatment evidence is based mainly on case reports and small case series rather than randomized trials; this concept does not prescribe a dose or monitoring interval.
claims.applicablePopulation: Stable adults with confirmed Felty syndrome who do not have an active infection and have not yet received syndrome-directed disease-modifying treatment.

claims.statement: Glucocorticoids or G-CSF may be used as temporary bridging or supportive therapy while disease-modifying treatment takes effect; glucocorticoids are not universally contraindicated but should be avoided in active infection and are not the preferred sole long-term strategy.
claims.limitation: The approved questions do not prescribe a dose, duration, laboratory target, or universal bridging regimen.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with confirmed Felty syndrome receiving specialist-directed treatment.

claims.statement: Splenectomy is generally reserved for Felty syndrome with recurrent infections despite adequate medical treatment rather than used as routine initial therapy.
claims.limitation: The exact likelihood and durability of hematologic response are not taught because the evidence is old, heterogeneous, and confounded by historical overlap with T-LGL leukemia.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with confirmed Felty syndrome and recurrent infections despite adequate specialist-directed medical therapy.

claims.statement: For the approved presentation of persistent anemia with biochemical hemolysis after documented total splenectomy, reassessment and evaluation for accessory splenic tissue is the selected next step.
claims.limitation: MCV or RDW alone does not establish persistent hemolysis, and this narrow teaching path does not diagnose every cause of anemia after splenectomy.
claims.applicablePopulation: Patients matching the approved hereditary-spherocytosis post-splenectomy presentations.

claims.statement: Absent Howell-Jolly bodies after splenectomy can support suspicion of residual functioning splenic tissue.
claims.limitation: Absence is supportive only; it is not independently diagnostic and is not sufficient to select surgery.
claims.applicablePopulation: Approved post-splenectomy hereditary-spherocytosis presentation with continued hemolysis.

claims.statement: Tc-99m heat-damaged RBC scintigraphy is the approved functional-tissue study for the constrained presentation after hereditary spherocytosis remains supported.
claims.limitation: The configured facility time is editorial game tuning rather than a clinical turnaround claim; this does not define a universal imaging sequence.
claims.applicablePopulation: Patients in the approved persistent-hemolysis functional-tissue evaluation presentation.

claims.statement: For the approved profile with confirmed functioning accessory splenic tissue causing persistent symptomatic hereditary-spherocytosis hemolysis, referral to hospital surgery for removal is the selected management disposition.
claims.limitation: Incidental tissue alone is not an indication, and this package does not simulate hospital surgery or endorse immediate reoperation before confirmation.
claims.applicablePopulation: Patients matching the confirmed, symptomatic, persistent-hemolysis profile in the approved management variants.

claims.statement: The approved pathway does not use steroids, IVIG, or embolization for persistent hereditary-spherocytosis hemolysis after splenectomy.

claims.applicablePopulation: The seven approved row-57 variants only.

claims.statement: For persistent ITP of only several months without severe bleeding and with feasible medical care, elective splenectomy should be deferred until at least one year after diagnosis when possible.

claims.applicablePopulation: Stable adults several months into persistent ITP with reliable hematology follow-up and no major bleeding.
